1.1: The beginning of the Good News of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 ha’Mashiaḥ, the Bĕn of Elohim.
1.2: As it has been written in the Neḇi’im, “See, I send My messenger before Your face, who shall prepare Your way before You,
1.3: a voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Prepare the way of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, make His paths straight.’ ”
1.4: Yoḥanan came immersing in the wilderness and proclaiming an immersion of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
1.5: And all the country of Yahuḏah, and those of Yerushalayim, went out to him and were all immersed by him in the Yardĕn River, confessing their sins.
1.6: And Yoḥanan was clothed with camel’s hair and a leather girdle around his waist, and eating locusts and wild honey.
1.7: And he proclaimed, saying, “After me comes One who is mightier than I, whose sandal strap I am not worthy to stoop down and loosen.
1.8: “I indeed immersed you in water, but He shall immerse you in the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh.”
1.9: And it came to be in those days that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 came from Natsareth of Galil, and was immersed by Yoḥanan in the Yardĕn.
1.10: And immediately, coming up from the water, He saw the shamayim being torn open and the Ruaḥ coming down on Him like a dove.
1.11: And a voice came out of the shamayim, “You are My Bĕn, the Beloved, in whom I delight.”
1.12: And immediately the Ruaḥ drove Him into the wilderness.
1.13: And He was there in the wilderness forty days, tried by Satan, and was with the wild beasts. And the messengers attended Him.
1.14: And after Yoḥanan was delivered up, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 came to Galil, proclaiming the Good News of the reign of Elohim,
1.15: and saying, “The time has been filled, and the Malḵuth of Elohim has come near. Repent, and believe in the Good News.”
1.16: And walking by the Sea of Galil, He saw Shim’on, and Andri his brother, casting a net into the sea, for they were fishers.
1.17: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to them, “Come, follow Me, and I shall make you become fishers of men.”
1.18: And immediately they left their nets and followed Him.
1.19: And having gone on a little from there, He saw Ya’aqoḇ, of Zaḇdai, and Yoḥanan his brother, and they were in the boat mending their nets.
1.20: And immediately He called them, and leaving their father Zaḇdai in the boat with the hired servants, they went after Him.
1.21: And they went into Kephar Naḥum, and immediately on the Shabbath He went into the congregation and taught.
1.22: And they were astonished at His teaching, for He was teaching them as possessing authority, and not as the scribes.
1.23: And there was a man in their congregation with an unclean spirit, and he cried out,
1.24: saying, “Ha! What have we to do with You, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 of Natsareth? Did You come to destroy us? I know who You are: the Qadosh One of Elohim!”
1.25: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 rebuked him, saying, “Be silenced, and come out of him!”
1.26: And throwing him into convulsions, the unclean spirit called out with a loud voice, and came out of him.
1.27: And they were all so amazed, as to reason among themselves, saying, “What is this, a fresh teaching? With authority He commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey Him!”
1.28: And news about Him immediately spread into all the country around Galil.
1.29: And coming out of the congregation, they went straight to the house of Shim’on and Andri, with Ya’aqoḇ and Yoḥanan.
1.30: And the mother-in-law of Shim’on lay sick with a fever, and immediately they spoke to Him about her.
1.31: And having come, He took her by the hand and lifted her up, and immediately the fever left her, and she served them.
1.32: And when evening came, when the sun was down, they brought to Him all who were sick and those who were demon-possessed.
1.33: And the entire city had gathered at the door.
1.34: And He healed many who were sick with various diseases, and cast out many demons, and was not allowing the demons to speak, because they knew Him.
1.35: And having risen very early in the morning, while still dim, He went out, and went away to a lonely place, and there He prayed.
1.36: And Shim’on and those who were with Him searched for Him,
1.37: and when they found Him, they said to Him, “All are seeking You.”
1.38: And He said to them, “Let us go into the neighboring towns, so that I proclaim there also, because for this I have come forth.”
1.39: And He was proclaiming in their congregations, in all Galil, and casting out demons.
1.40: And a leper came to Him, calling upon Him, kneeling down to Him and saying to Him, “If You desire, You are able to make me clean.”
1.41: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, moved with compassion, stretched out His hand and touched him, and said to him, “I desire it. Be cleansed.”
1.42: And immediately the leprosy left him, and he was cleansed.
1.43: And having strictly warned him, He immediately sent him away,
1.44: and said to him, “See, say naught to anyone, but go show yourself to the kohĕn, and offer for your cleansing what Mosheh ordered, as a witness to them.”
1.45: But he went out and began to publish it so much, and to spread the word, that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 was no longer able to openly enter the city, but was outside in lonely places. Yet they came to Him from all directions.

10.1: And rising up from there He came into the borders of Yahuḏah by the other side of the Yardĕn. And crowds gathered to Him again, and as He usually did, He was teaching them again.
10.2: And Pharisees came and asked Him, “Is it right for a man to put away his wife?” - trying Him.
10.3: And He answering, said to them, “What did Mosheh command you?”
10.4: And they said, “Mosheh allowed a man to write a certificate of separation, and to divorce.”
10.5: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to them, “Because of the hardness of your heart he wrote you this command.
10.6: “However, from the beginning of the creation, Elohim ‘made them male and female.’
10.7: ‘For this cause a man shall leave his father and mother and join unto his wife,
10.8: and the two shall become one flesh,’ so that they are no longer two, but one flesh.
10.9: “Therefore what Elohim has joined together, let man not separate.”
10.10: And in the house His talmidim asked Him about this again.
10.11: And He said to them, “Whoever puts away his wife and marries another commits adultery against her.
10.12: “And if a woman puts away her husband and marries another, she commits adultery.”
10.13: And they were bringing little children for Him to touch them, but the talmidim were rebuking those who were bringing them.
10.14: And when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 saw it, He was much displeased and said to them, “Let the little children come to Me, and do not forbid them, for of such is the Malḵuth of Elohim.
10.15: “Truly, I say to you, whoever does not receive the Malḵuth of Elohim as a little child, shall certainly not enter into it.”
10.16: And taking them up in His arms, laying His hands on them, He baraḵ them.
10.17: And as He was proceeding on the way, one came running, and knelt before Him, and asked Him, “Good Teacher, what shall I do to inherit everlasting ḥai?”
10.18: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to him, “Why do you call Me good? No one is good except One - Elohim.
10.19: “You know the Commands, ‘Do not commit adultery,’ ‘Do not murder,’ ‘Do not steal,’ ‘Do not bear false witness,’ ‘Do not defraud,’ ‘Respect your father and your mother.’ ”
10.20: And he answering, said to Him, “Teacher, all these I have watched over from my youth.”
10.21: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, looking at him, loved him, and said to him, “One you lack: Go, sell all you possess and give to the poor, and you shall have treasure in the shamayim. And come, follow Me, taking up the stake.”
10.22: But he, being sad at this word, went away grieved, for he had many possessions.
10.23: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, looking around, said to His talmidim, “How hard it is for those who have riches to enter into the Malḵuth of Elohim!”
10.24: And the talmidim were astonished at His words. And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 responding, said to them again, “Children, how hard it is for those who trust in riches to enter into the Malḵuth of Elohim!
10.25: “It is easier for a camel to enter through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter into the Malḵuth of Elohim.”
10.26: And they were immeasurably astonished, saying among themselves, “Who then is able to be saved?”
10.27: And looking at them, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said, “With men it is impossible, but not with Elohim, for with Elohim all is possible.”
10.28: And Kĕpha began to say to Him, “See, we have left all and we have followed You.”
10.29: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said, “Truly, I say to you, there is no one who has left house or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or lands, for the sake of Me and the Good News,
10.30: who shall not receive a hundredfold now in this time, houses and brothers and sisters and mothers and children and lands, with persecutions, and in the age to come, everlasting ḥai.
10.31: “But many who are first shall be last, and the last first.”
10.32: And they were on the way, going up to Yerushalayim, and 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 was going before them. And they were astonished, and those who followed were afraid. And again He took the twelve aside and began to say to them what was about to befall Him:
10.33: “See, we are going up to Yerushalayim, and the Bĕn of Aḏam shall be delivered to the chief kohenim and to the scribes, and they shall condemn Him to death and shall deliver Him to the gentiles,
10.34: and they shall mock Him, and flog Him, and spit on Him, and kill Him. And the third day He shall rise again.”
10.35: And Ya’aqoḇ and Yoḥanan, the sons of Zaḇdai, came up to Him, saying, “Teacher, we want You to do for us whatever we ask.”
10.36: And He said to them, “What do you want Me to do for you?”
10.37: And they said to Him, “Grant us to be seated in Your esteem, one on Your right hand and the other on Your left.”
10.38: But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to them, “You do not know what you ask. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink, and be immersed with the immersion that I am immersed with?”
10.39: And they said to Him, “We are able.” And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to them, “You shall indeed drink the cup that I drink, and with the immersion I am immersed with, you shall be immersed,
10.40: but to sit on My right hand and on My left is not Mine to give, but it is for those for whom it has been prepared.”
10.41: And when the ten heard it, they began to be sorely displeased with Ya’aqoḇ and Yoḥanan.
10.42: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, calling them near, said to them, “You know that those who think to rule the gentiles are masters over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.
10.43: “But it is not so among you, but whoever wants to become great among you shall be your servant.
10.44: “And whoever wants to be first among you, shall be servant of all.
10.45: “For even the Bĕn of Aḏam did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His ḥai a ransom for many.”
10.46: And they came to Yeriḥo. And as He was leaving Yeriḥo with His talmidim and a large crowd, blind Bartimai, the son of Timai, was sitting by the way begging.
10.47: And when he heard that it was 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 of Natsareth, he began to cry out and to say, “𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 Bĕn of Dawiḏ, have compassion on me!”
10.48: And many were reprimanding him to be silent, but he cried out all the more, “Bĕn of Dawiḏ, have compassion on me!”
10.49: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 stopped and said, “Call him.” And they called the blind man, saying to him, “Take courage, arise, He is calling you.”
10.50: And he, throwing aside his garment, rose and came to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
10.51: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 responding, said to him, “What do you desire I do for you?” And the blind man said to Him, “Rabboni, that I receive my sight.”
10.52: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to him, “Go, your belief has healed you.” And immediately he saw again and followed 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 on the way.

11.1: And when they came near Yerushalayim, to Bĕyth Phaḡi and Bĕyth Anyah, at the Mount of Olives, He sent out two of His talmidim,
11.2: and said to them, “Go into the village opposite you, and immediately entering into it, you shall find a colt tied, on which no one has sat. Loosen it and bring it.
11.3: “And if anyone says to you, ‘Why are you doing this?’ say, ‘The Aḏon needs it and shall send it back here straightaway.’ ”
11.4: So they went away, and found the colt tied by the door outside on the street, and they loosened it.
11.5: And some of those standing there said to them, “What are you doing, loosening the colt?”
11.6: And they said to them, as 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 had said. So they let them go.
11.7: And they brought the colt to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 and threw their garments on it, and He sat on it.
11.8: And many spread their garments on the way, and others were cutting down branches from the trees and were spreading them on the way.
11.9: And those going before and those following cried out, saying, “Hoshia-na! ‘Baruḵ is He who is coming in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄!’
11.10: Beruḵah is the coming Malḵuth of our father Dawiḏ - in the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Hoshia-na in the highest!”
11.11: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 went into Yerushalayim and into the Miqdash. And having looked around on all, He went out to Bĕyth Anyah with the twelve, as the hour was already late.
11.12: And on the next day, when they had come out from Bĕyth Anyah, He was hungry.
11.13: And seeing at a distance a fig tree having leaves, He went to see whether He would find anything on it. And when He came to it, He found naught but leaves, for it was not the season for figs.
11.14: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, responding, said to it, “Let no one eat fruit from you ever again.” And His talmidim heard it.
11.15: And they came to Yerushalayim. 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, entering into the Miqdash, began to drive out those who bought and sold in the Miqdash, and overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves.
11.16: And He did not allow anyone to carry a vessel through the Miqdash.
11.17: And He was teaching, saying to them, “Has it not been written, ‘My House shall be called a house of prayer for all nations’? But you have made it a ‘den of robbers.’ ”
11.18: And the scribes and the chief kohenim heard it and they were seeking how to destroy Him, for they feared Him, because all the crowd was astonished at His teaching.
11.19: And when evening came, He went out of the city.
11.20: And in the morning, passing by, they saw the fig tree dried up from the roots.
11.21: Then Kĕpha, remembering, said to Him, “Rabbi, look! The fig tree which You cursed has withered.”
11.22: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answering, said to them, “Have belief in Elohim.
11.23: “For truly, I say to you, whoever says to this mountain, ‘Be removed and be thrown into the sea,’ and does not doubt in his heart, but believes that what he says, shall be done, he shall have whatever he says.
11.24: “Because of this I say to you, whatever you ask when you pray, believe that you receive them, and you shall have them.
11.25: “And whenever you stand praying, if you hold whatever against anyone, forgive, so that your Father in the shamayim shall also forgive you your trespasses.
11.26: “But if you do not forgive, neither shall your Father in the shamayim forgive your trespasses.”
11.27: And they came again to Yerushalayim. And as He was walking in the Miqdash, the chief kohenim, and the scribes, and the elders came to Him,
11.28: and they said to Him, “By what authority are You doing these? And who gave You this authority to do these?”
11.29: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answering, said to them, “I shall ask you one question, and answer Me, and I shall say to you by what authority I do these:
11.30: “The immersion of Yoḥanan - was it from the shamayim or from men? Answer Me.”
11.31: And they reasoned among themselves, saying, “If we say, ‘From the shamayim,’ He shall say, ‘Then why did you not believe him?’
11.32: “But if we say, ‘From men’ ” - they feared the people, for all held that Yoḥanan was a naḇi indeed.
11.33: And answering they said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, “We do not know.” And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answering, said to them, “Neither do I say to you by what authority I do these.”

12.1: And He began to speak to them in parables, “A man planted a vineyard and put a hedge around it, and dug a vat for the winepress and built a watchtower, and let it out to farmers and went away.
12.2: “And in due season he sent a servant to the farmers, to receive some of the fruit of the vineyard from the farmers.
12.3: “And they seized and beat him and sent away empty-handed.
12.4: “And again he sent them another servant, and throwing stones, they wounded him in the head, and having insulted, sent him away.
12.5: “And again he sent another, and they killed him; and many others, beating some and killing some.
12.6: “He had one more son, his beloved. He sent him to them last of all, saying, ‘They shall respect my son.’
12.7: “But those farmers said among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance shall be ours.’
12.8: “So they took and killed him and threw him out of the vineyard.
12.9: “What then shall the owner of the vineyard do? He shall come and destroy the farmers, and give the vineyard to others.
12.10: “Have you not read this Scripture, ‘The Stone which the builders rejected has become the chief Corner-Stone.
12.11: ‘This was from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and it is marvelous in our eyes’?”
12.12: And they were seeking to seize Him, but feared the crowd, for they knew He had spoken the parable against them. And leaving Him, they went away.
12.13: And they sent to Him some of the Pharisees and the Hĕrodians, to catch Him in a word.
12.14: And when they came, they said to Him, “Teacher, we know that You are true, and it does not concern You about anyone, for You are not partial to any, but teach the Way of Elohim in truth. Is it right to pay taxes to Kaisar, or not?
12.15: “Should we pay, or should we not pay?” And He, knowing their hypocrisy, said to them, “Why do you try Me? Bring Me a silver piece to look at.”
12.16: And they brought it, and He said to them, “Whose likeness and inscription is this?” And they said to Him, “Kaisar’s.”
12.17: So 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to them, “Give to Kaisar what is Kaisar’s, and to Elohim what is Elohim’s.” And they marveled at Him.
12.18: And Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to Him. And they asked Him, saying,
12.19: “Teacher, Mosheh wrote to us that if a brother of anyone dies, and leaves his wife behind, and leaves no children, his brother should take his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
12.20: “There were seven brothers, and the first took a wife, and died, leaving no offspring.
12.21: “And the second took her, and he died, leaving behind no offspring. And the third likewise.
12.22: “And the seven left no offspring. Last of all the woman died too.
12.23: “In the resurrection then, when they rise, whose wife shall she be? For seven had her as wife.”
12.24: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answering, said to them, “Is this not why you go astray, because you do not know the Scriptures nor the power of Elohim?
12.25: “For when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are as messengers in the shamayim.
12.26: “And concerning the dead, that they rise - have you not read in the Book of Mosheh, at the bush, how Elohim spoke to him, saying, ‘I am the Elohim of Aḇraham, and the Elohim of Yitsḥaq, and the Elohim of Ya’aqoḇ’?
12.27: “He is not the Elohim of the dead, but Elohim of the living. You, then, go greatly astray.”
12.28: And one of the scribes coming near, hearing them reasoning together, knowing that He had answered them well, asked Him, “Which is the first Command of all?”
12.29: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answered him, “The first of all the Commands is, ‘Hear, O Yisra’ĕl, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is one.
12.30: ‘And you shall love 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 your Elohim with all your heart, and with all your being, and with all your mind, and with all your strength.’ This is the first Command.
12.31: “And the second, like it, is this, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other command greater than these.”
12.32: And the scribe said to Him, “Well said, Teacher. You have spoken the truth, for there is one Elohim, and there is no other besides Him.
12.33: “And to love Him with all the heart, and with all the understanding, and with all the being, and with all the strength, and to love one’s neighbor as oneself, is more than all the burnt offerings and slaughter offerings.”
12.34: And when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 saw that he answered wisely, He said to him, “You are not far from the Malḵuth of Elohim.” And after that no one dared to question Him.
12.35: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 responding, said, while teaching in the Miqdash, “How is it that the scribes say that ha’Mashiaḥ is the Bĕn of Dawiḏ?
12.36: “Dawiḏ himself said by the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh, ‘𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 said to Aḏoni, “Sit at My right hand, until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.” ’
12.37: “Dawiḏ himself calls Him ‘Aḏoni.’ In what way then is He his Bĕn?” And the large crowd heard Him gladly.
12.38: And in His teaching He was saying to them, “Beware of the scribes, who like to walk around in long robes, and greetings in the market-places,
12.39: and the best seats in the congregations, and the best places at feasts,
12.40: who are devouring widows’ houses, and for a show make long prayers. These shall receive greater judgment.”
12.41: And sitting opposite the treasury He saw how the people put copper into the treasury. And many rich ones put in much.
12.42: And a poor widow came and threw in two small coins, which amount to a quarter.
12.43: And calling near His talmidim He said to them, “Truly, I say to you that this poor widow has put in more than all those putting into the treasury,
12.44: for they all put in out of their excess, but she out of her poverty put in all that she had, her entire livelihood.”

13.1: And as He went out of the Miqdash, one of His talmidim said to Him, “Teacher, see what stones! And what buildings!”
13.2: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answering, said to him, “Do you see these great buildings? Not one stone shall be left upon another at all, which shall not be thrown down.”
13.3: And as He sat on the Mount of Olives opposite the Miqdash, Kĕpha, and Ya’aqoḇ, and Yoḥanan, and Andri asked Him separately,
13.4: “Say to us, when shall these be? And what shall be the sign when all this is going to be accomplished?”
13.5: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 began to say to them, “Take heed that no one leads you astray,
13.6: for many shall come in My Name, saying, ‘I am He,’ and they shall lead many astray.
13.7: “And when you hear of fightings and reports of fightings, do not be troubled - it has to take place, but the end is not yet.
13.8: “For nation shall rise against nation, and malḵuth against malḵuth. And there shall be earthquakes in various places, and there shall be scarcities of food, and disturbances. These are the beginnings of birth-pains.
13.9: “But take heed to yourselves, for they shall deliver you up to councils and to congregations. You shall be beaten, and you shall be brought before rulers and melaḵim for My sake, for a witness to them.
13.10: “And the Good News has to be proclaimed first to all the nations.
13.11: “And when they lead you away and deliver you up, do not worry beforehand what you are to say. But whatever is given you in that hour, speak that, for it is not you who are speaking, but the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh.
13.12: “And brother shall deliver up brother to death, and a father his child. And children shall rise up against parents and shall put them to death.
13.13: “And you shall be hated by all because of My Name. But he who shall have endured to the end, he shall be saved.
13.14: “And when you see the ‘abomination that lays waste,’ spoken of by Dani’ĕl the naḇi, put up where it should not be” - he who reads, let him understand - “then let those who are in Yahuḏah flee to the mountains.
13.15: “And he who is on the house-top, let him not go down into the house, nor come in to take whatever out of his house.
13.16: “And he who is in the field, let him not go back to get his cloak.
13.17: “And woe to those who are pregnant and to those nursing children in those days!
13.18: “And pray that your flight does not take place in winter.
13.19: “For in those days there shall be distress, such as has not been from the beginning of creation which Elohim created until this time, nor ever shall be.
13.20: “And if the Aḏon had not shortened those days, no flesh would have been saved; but because of the chosen ones, whom He chose, He shortened the days.
13.21: “And if anyone then says to you, ‘Look, here is ha’Mashiaḥ!’ or, ‘Look, there!’ do not believe it.
13.22: “For false messiahs and false prophets shall rise and show signs and wonders to lead astray, if possible, even the chosen ones.
13.23: “And you, take heed. See, I have forewarned you of it all.
13.24: “But in those days, after that distress, the sun shall be darkened, and the moon shall not give its light,
13.25: and the stars of the shamayim shall fall, and the powers in the shamayim shall be shaken.
13.26: “And then they shall see the Bĕn of Aḏam coming in the clouds with much power and esteem.
13.27: “And then He shall send His messengers, and assemble His chosen ones from the four winds, from the farthest part of earth to the farthest part of the shamayim.
13.28: “And learn this parable from the fig tree: When its branch has already become tender, and puts forth leaves, you know that the summer is near.
13.29: “So you also, when you see these taking place, know that it is near, at the door.
13.30: “Truly, I say to you, this generation shall by no means pass away till all this takes place.
13.31: “The shamayim and the earth shall pass away, but My Words shall by no means pass away.
13.32: “But concerning that day and the hour no one knows, not even the messengers in the shamayim, nor the Bĕn, but only the Father.
13.33: “Take heed, watch and pray, for you do not know when the time is -
13.34: as a man going abroad, having left his house and given authority to his servants, and to each his work, and commanded the doorkeeper to watch.
13.35: “Watch therefore, for you do not know when the master of the house is coming - in the evening or at midnight, or at the crowing of the cock, or in the morning,
13.36: lest, coming suddenly, he should find you sleeping.
13.37: “And what I say to you, I say to all: Watch!”

14.1: Now the Pesaḥ and Matstsoth was after two days. And the chief kohenim and the scribes were seeking how to take Him through treachery and put Him to death.
14.2: And they said, “Not at the Festival, lest there shall be an uproar of the people.”
14.3: And while He was in Bĕyth Anyah in the house of Shim’on the leper, and sitting at the table, a woman came having an alabaster flask of perfume, genuine nard, very costly. And breaking the flask she poured it on His head.
14.4: But there were some who were much displeased among themselves, and said, “Why was this perfume wasted?
14.5: “For it could have been sold for more than three hundred pieces of silver and given to the poor.” And they were scolding her.
14.6: But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said, “Leave her alone. Why do you trouble her? She has done a good work for Me.
14.7: “For you have the poor with you always, and whenever you want, you are able to do good to them. But you do not always have Me.
14.8: “What she could, she did. She came beforehand to anoint My body for the burial.
14.9: “Truly, I say to you, wherever this Good News is proclaimed in all the world, what this woman did shall also be spoken of, to her remembrance.”
14.10: And Yahuḏah from Qeriyoth, one of the twelve, went to the chief kohenim to deliver Him up to them.
14.11: And when they heard it, they were glad, and promised to give him silver. And he was seeking how to deliver Him up, conveniently.
14.12: And on the first day of Matstsoth, when they were slaughtering the Pesaḥ, His talmidim said to Him, “Where do You want us to go and prepare, for You to eat the Pesaḥ?”
14.13: And He sent out two of His talmidim and said to them, “Go into the city, and there a man bearing a jar of water shall meet you, follow him.
14.14: “And wherever he enters, say to the master of the house, ‘The Teacher says, “Where is the guest room in which I am to eat the Pesaḥ with My talmidim?” ’
14.15: “And he shall show you a large upper room, furnished, ready. Prepare for us there.”
14.16: And His talmidim went out and came into the city, and found it as He said to them, and they prepared the Pesaḥ.
14.17: And evening having come, He came with the twelve.
14.18: And as they sat and ate, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said, “Truly, I say to you, one of you who is eating with Me shall deliver Me up.”
14.19: And they began to be grieved, and to say to Him one by one, “Is it I?” And another, “Is it I?”
14.20: And He answering, said to them, “It is one of the twelve, he who is dipping with Me in the dish.
14.21: “The Bĕn of Aḏam is indeed going, as it has been written of Him, but woe to that man by whom the Bĕn of Aḏam is delivered up! It would have been good for that man if he had not been born.”
14.22: And as they were eating, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 took bread, having baraḵ, broke it, gave it to them and said, “Take, eat, this is My body.”
14.23: And taking the cup, giving thanks, He gave it to them, and they all drank from it.
14.24: And He said to them, “This is My blood, that of the Renewed Covenant, which is shed for many.
14.25: “Truly, I say to you, I shall certainly no more drink of the fruit of the vine till that day when I drink it anew in the Malḵuth of Elohim.”
14.26: And having sung a song, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
14.27: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to them, “All of you shall stumble in Me this night, for it has been written, ‘I shall strike the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered.’
14.28: “But after I am raised, I shall go before you to Galil.”
14.29: And Kĕpha said to Him, “Even if all shall stumble, yet not I.”
14.30: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to him, “Truly, I say to you that today, this night, before the cock shall crow twice, you shall deny Me three times.”
14.31: But he spoke more strongly, “If I have to die with You, I shall not deny You!” And they all said the same.
14.32: And they came to a place called Gath Shemen. And He said to His talmidim, “Sit here while I pray.”
14.33: And He took with Him Kĕpha, and Ya’aqoḇ, and Yoḥanan, and He began to be greatly alarmed, and to be deeply distressed.
14.34: And He said to them, “My being is exceedingly grieved, even to death. Stay here and watch.”
14.35: And He went on a little, and fell on the ground, and was praying that if it were possible, the hour might pass from Him.
14.36: And He said, “Abba, Father, all is possible for You. Make this cup pass from Me. Yet not what I desire, but what You.”
14.37: And He came and found them sleeping, and said to Kĕpha, “Shim’on, are you sleeping? You were not able to watch one hour!
14.38: “Watch and pray, lest you enter into trial. The spirit indeed is eager, but the flesh is weak.”
14.39: And again He went away and prayed, and spoke the same words.
14.40: And having returned, He found them asleep again, for their eyes were heavy. And they did not know what to answer Him.
14.41: And He came the third time and said to them, “Are you still sleeping and resting? It is enough! The hour has come. See, the Bĕn of Aḏam is being delivered up into the hands of the sinners.
14.42: “Rise up, let us go. See, he who is delivering Me up has drawn near.”
14.43: And immediately, while He was still speaking, Yahuḏah, one of the twelve, with a large crowd with swords and clubs, came from the chief kohenim and the scribes and the elders.
14.44: And the one who was delivering Him up had given them a signal, saying, “Whomever I kiss, it is He - seize Him and lead Him away safely.”
14.45: And coming, going straight up to Him, he said to Him, “Rabbi, Rabbi!” and kissed Him.
14.46: And they laid their hands on Him and seized Him.
14.47: And one of those standing by drew his sword and struck the servant of the kohĕn ha’gadol, and cut off his ear.
14.48: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 answering, said to them, “Have you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs, to take Me?
14.49: “Daily I was with you in the Miqdash teaching, and you did not seize Me. But let the Scriptures be filled.”
14.50: And they all left Him and fled.
14.51: And a certain young man was following Him, having a linen cloth over his nakedness. And when they seized him,
14.52: he left the linen cloth and fled from them naked.
14.53: And they led 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 away to the kohĕn ha’gadol. And all the chief kohenim, and the elders, and the scribes came together to Him.
14.54: And Kĕpha followed Him at a distance, even into the courtyard of the kohĕn ha’gadol. And he was sitting with the officers and warming himself at the fire.
14.55: And the chief kohenim and all the council were seeking witness against 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 to put Him to death, and they were finding none.
14.56: For many bore false witness against Him, but their evidences did not agree.
14.57: And some rose up and bore false witness against Him, saying,
14.58: “We heard Him saying, ‘I shall destroy this Mishkan that is made with hands, and within three days I shall build another made without hands.’ ”
14.59: And not even then did their witness agree.
14.60: Then the kohĕn ha’gadol stood up in the center and asked 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, saying, “Have You no answer to make? What do these witness against You?”
14.61: But He remained silent and gave no answer. Again the kohĕn ha’gadol asked Him, saying to Him, “Are You ha’Mashiaḥ, the Bĕn of the Baruḵ?”
14.62: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said, “I am, and you shall see the Bĕn of Aḏam sitting at the right hand of the Almighty, and coming with the clouds of the shamayim.”
14.63: And tearing his garments, the kohĕn ha’gadol said, “What further need do we have of witnesses?
14.64: “You have heard the blasphemy! What do you think?” And they all condemned Him to be liable to death.
14.65: And some began to spit on Him, and to blindfold Him, and to beat Him, and to say to Him, “Naḇa!” And the officers struck Him with the palms of their hands.
14.66: And as Kĕpha was below in the courtyard, one of the servant girls of the kohĕn ha’gadol came,
14.67: and seeing Kĕpha warming himself, she looked at him and said, “And you were with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 of Natsareth.”
14.68: But he denied it, saying, “I do not know nor understand what you are saying.” And he went out onto the porch, and a cock crowed.
14.69: And the servant girl saw him again, and began to say to those who stood by, “This is one of them.”
14.70: And again he was denying it. And after a little while those who stood by again said to Kĕpha, “Truly you are one of them, for you are a Galilean too, and your speech is alike.”
14.71: And he began to curse and swear, “I do not know this Man of whom you speak!”
14.72: And a second time the cock crowed. And Kĕpha remembered the word that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 had said to him, “Before the cock crows twice, you shall deny Me three times.” And thinking on it, he wept.

15.1: And immediately, in the morning, the chief kohenim took counsel with the elders and scribes and all the council. Having bound 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, they led Him away, and delivered Him to Pilatus.
15.2: And Pilatus asked Him, “You are the Meleḵ of the Yahuḏim?” And He answering, said to him, “You say it.”
15.3: And the chief kohenim accused Him of much, but He made no answer.
15.4: And Pilatus again asked Him, saying, “Have You no answer? See how much they witness against You!”
15.5: But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 still gave no answer, so that Pilatus marveled.
15.6: And at a Festival he released to them one prisoner, whomever they were asking.
15.7: And there was one called Barabba, chained with his fellow rebels, who had committed murder in the uprising.
15.8: And the crowd, crying aloud, began to ask, as he had always done for them.
15.9: But Pilatus answered them, saying, “Do you want me to release for you the Meleḵ of the Yahuḏim?”
15.10: For he knew that the chief kohenim had handed Him over because of envy.
15.11: And the chief kohenim stirred up the crowd, that he should rather release Barabba to them.
15.12: And Pilatus answered and again said to them, “What then do you want me to do to whom you call the Meleḵ of the Yahuḏim?”
15.13: And again they cried out, “Impale Him!”
15.14: And Pilatus said to them, “Why, what evil has He done?” And they vehemently cried out, “Impale Him!”
15.15: And Pilatus, wanting to satisfy the crowd, released Barabba to them, and having whipped, he delivered 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 over to be impaled.
15.16: And the soldiers led Him away into the court, which is the palace, and they called together the entire cohort,
15.17: and decked Him with purple. And they plaited a crown of thorns, put it on Him,
15.18: and they began to call out to Him, “Greetings, Meleḵ of the Yahuḏim!”
15.19: And they kept beating Him on the head with a reed and were spitting on Him. And bending the knee, they were bowing down to Him.
15.20: And when they had mocked Him, they took the purple off Him, and put His own garments on Him, and led Him out to impale Him.
15.21: And they compelled a passer-by, Shim’on, a Kurĕnaion, coming from a field, the father of Alexandros and Rufus, to bear His stake.
15.22: And they brought Him to the place Golgotha, which is translated, Place of a Skull.
15.23: And they were giving Him wine mixed with myrrh to drink, but He did not take it.
15.24: And when they impaled Him, they divided His garments, casting lots for them, what each one should take.
15.25: And it was the third hour, and they impaled Him.
15.26: And the inscription of His accusation was written above: THE MELEḴ OF THE YAHUḎIM.
15.27: And with Him they impaled two robbers, one on His right and the other on His left.
15.28: And the Scripture was filled which says, “And He was reckoned with the lawless.”
15.29: And those passing by were blaspheming Him, shaking their heads and saying, “Ah! You who destroy the Mishkan and build it in three days,
15.30: save Yourself, and come down from the stake!”
15.31: And likewise the chief kohenim and the scribes, mocking to one another said, “He saved others, He is unable to save Himself.
15.32: “Let ha’Mashiaḥ, the Meleḵ of Yisra’ĕl, come down now from the stake, so that we see and believe.” And those who were impaled with Him were reproaching Him.
15.33: And when the sixth hour came, darkness came over all the land until the ninth hour.
15.34: And at the ninth hour 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 cried out with a loud voice, saying, “Ĕli, Ĕli, lamah sheḇaqtani?” which is translated, “My Ĕl, My Ĕl, why have You forsaken Me?”
15.35: And some of those standing by, when they heard it, said, “See, He is calling for Ĕliyahu!”
15.36: And someone ran and filled a sponge with vinegar, and put it on a reed, and offered it to Him to drink, saying, “Leave Him, let us see if Ĕliyahu comes to take Him down.”
15.37: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 cried out with a loud voice, and breathed His last.
15.38: And the veil of the Mishkan was torn in two from top to bottom.
15.39: And when the captain, who was standing opposite Him, saw that He cried out like this and breathed His last, he said, “Truly this Man was the Bĕn of Elohim!”
15.40: And there were also women watching from a distance, among whom was also Miryam from Maḡdala, and Miryam the mother of Ya’aqoḇ the Less and of Yosĕph, and Shelomah,
15.41: who also followed Him and attended Him when He was in Galil, and many other women who came up with Him to Yerushalayim.
15.42: And when evening had come, because it was the Preparation Day, that is, the day before the Shabbath,
15.43: Yosĕph of Ramathayim, a prominent council member, who was himself waiting for the Malḵuth of Elohim, came, boldly went in to Pilatus and asked for the body of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
15.44: But Pilatus wondered whether He was already dead, so summoning the captain, he asked him if He was already dead.
15.45: And when he learned from the captain, he gave the body to Yosĕph.
15.46: And he, having bought fine linen, took Him down, and wrapped Him in the linen. And he laid Him in a tomb which had been hewn out of the rock, and rolled a stone against the entrance of the tomb.
15.47: And Miryam from Maḡdala, and Miryam of Yosĕph, saw where He was laid.

16.1: And when the Shabbath was past, Miryam from Maḡdala, and Miryam of Ya’aqoḇ, and Shelomah bought spices, to go and anoint Him.
16.2: And very early morning, on one of the shabbathoth, they came to the tomb when the sun had risen.
16.3: And they said among themselves, “Who shall roll away the stone from the entrance of the tomb for us?”
16.4: And looking up, they saw that the stone had been rolled away, for it was extremely large.
16.5: And having entered into the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right, wearing a white robe, and they were greatly alarmed.
16.6: And he said to them, “Do not be much alarmed. You seek 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 of Natsareth, who was impaled. He is raised - He is not here! See the place where they laid Him.
16.7: “And go, say to His talmidim, and Kĕpha, that He is going before you into Galil. You shall see Him there as He said to you.”
16.8: And they went out and fled from the tomb, and were trembling and bewildered. And they spoke to no one, for they were afraid.
16.9: And having risen in the morning on the first day of the week, He appeared first to Miryam from Maḡdala, from whom He had cast out seven demons.
16.10: She went and reported to those who had been with Him, mourning and weeping.
16.11: And when they heard that He was alive and had been seen by her, they did not believe.
16.12: And after this He appeared in another form to two of them as they walked and went into a field.
16.13: And they went and reported it to the rest, but they did not believe them either.
16.14: Later He appeared to the eleven as they sat at the table. And He reproached their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they did not believe those who had seen Him after He was raised.
16.15: And He said to them, “Go into all the world and proclaim the Good News to every creature.
16.16: “He who has believed and has been immersed, shall be saved, but he who has not believed shall be condemned.
16.17: “And these signs shall accompany the ones who believe: In My Name they shall cast out demons, they shall speak with renewed tongues,
16.18: they shall take up snakes, and if they drink anything deadly it shall by no means hurt them, they shall lay hands on the sick and they shall get well.”
16.19: Then indeed, after the Aḏon had spoken to them, He was received up into the shamayim, and sat down at the right hand of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
16.20: And they went out and proclaimed it everywhere, while the Aḏon worked with them, and confirmed the Word through the accompanying signs. Amĕn.

2.1: And some days later He again entered into Kephar Naḥum, and it was heard that He was in the house.
2.2: And so many gathered together, that there was no more room, not even at the door. And He spoke the Word to them.
2.3: And they came to Him, bringing a paralytic, carried by four.
2.4: And not being able to come near Him because of the crowd, they uncovered the roof where He was. And when they had broken through, they let down the bed on which the paralytic was lying.
2.5: And when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 saw their belief, He said to the paralytic, “Son, your sins are forgiven you.”
2.6: Now some of the scribes were sitting there, and reasoning in their hearts,
2.7: “Why does this One talk like this? He is blaspheming! Who is able to forgive sins but Elohim alone?”
2.8: And immediately 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, knowing in His spirit that they were reasoning that way within themselves, said to them, “Why do you reason about all this in your hearts?
2.9: “Which is easier, to say to the paralytic, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Rise, take up your bed and walk’?
2.10: “But in order for you to know that the Bĕn of Aḏam possesses authority on earth to forgive sins...” He said to the paralytic,
2.11: “I say to you, rise, take up your bed, and go to your house.”
2.12: And he rose straightaway, and took up the bed, and went out before all, so that all were amazed and praised Elohim, saying, “We have never seen the like of it!”
2.13: And He went out again by the sea, and all the crowd was coming to Him, and He taught them.
2.14: And passing by, He saw Lĕwi of Ḥĕleph sitting at the tax office, and said to him, “Follow Me.” And having risen he followed Him.
2.15: And it came to be, as He sat at the table at his house, that many tax collectors and sinners also sat with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 and His talmidim, for there were many, and they followed Him.
2.16: And when the scribes and Pharisees saw Him eating with the tax collectors and sinners, they said to His talmidim, “Why does He eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?”
2.17: And hearing this, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to them, “Those who are strong have no need of a physician, but those who are sick. I did not come to call the righteous to repentance, but sinners.”
2.18: And the talmidim of Yoḥanan and of the Pharisees were fasting. And they came and said to Him, “Why do the talmidim of Yoḥanan and of the Pharisees fast, but Your talmidim do not fast?”
2.19: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to them, “Are the friends of the bridegroom able to fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them they are not able to fast.
2.20: “But the days shall come when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then they shall fast in those days.
2.21: “And no one sews a piece of unshrunk cloth on an old garment, otherwise, the renewed piece pulls away from the old, and the tear is made worse.
2.22: “And no one puts new wine into old wineskins, otherwise the new wine bursts the wineskins, and the wine runs out, and the wineskins are ruined. But new wine is to be put into fresh wineskins.”
2.23: And it came to be that He went through the grainfields on the Shabbath. And as they went His talmidim began to pluck heads of grain,
2.24: and the Pharisees said to Him, “Look, why do they do what is not right on the Shabbath?”
2.25: And He said to them, “Have you never read what Dawiḏ did when he had need and was hungry, he and those with him?
2.26: “How he went into the House of Elohim, while Eḇyathar was kohĕn ha’gadol, and ate the showbread, which is not right to eat, except for the kohenim, and he gave it also to those who were with him?”
2.27: And He said to them, “The Shabbath was made for man, and not man for the Shabbath.
2.28: “So the Bĕn of Aḏam is also Aḏon of the Shabbath.”

3.1: And He went into the congregation again, and a man who had a withered hand was there.
3.2: And they were closely watching Him, whether He would heal him on the Shabbath, so as to accuse Him.
3.3: And He said to the man who had the withered hand, “Get up to the middle.”
3.4: And He said to them, “Is it right to do good on the Shabbath, or to do evil, to save life or to kill?” But they remained silent.
3.5: And having looked around on them with displeasure, being grieved at the hardness of their hearts, He said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” And he stretched it out, and his hand was restored as healthy as the other.
3.6: And the Pharisees went out and immediately plotted with the Hĕrodians against Him, how to destroy Him.
3.7: But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 withdrew with His talmidim to the sea. And a great crowd from Galil followed Him, and from Yahuḏah.
3.8: Even from Yerushalayim, and from Eḏom and beyond the Yardĕn, and those around Tsor and Tsiḏon, a large crowd came to Him when they heard how much He was doing.
3.9: And He spoke to His talmidim, that a small boat should be kept ready for Him because of the crowd, lest they should press upon Him.
3.10: For He healed many, so that as many as had afflictions fell upon Him to touch Him.
3.11: And the unclean spirits, whenever they saw Him, fell down before Him and cried out, saying, “You are the Bĕn of Elohim.”
3.12: But He warned them many times that they should not make Him known.
3.13: And He went up on the mountain and called to Him whom He wanted, and they came to Him.
3.14: And He appointed twelve to be with Him, and to be sent out to proclaim,
3.15: and to possess authority to heal sicknesses and to cast out demons.
3.16: And He appointed the twelve: Shim’on, to whom He added the name Kĕpha;
3.17: and Ya’aqoḇ of Zaḇdai, and Yoḥanan the brother of Ya’aqoḇ, to whom He added the name, Benĕy Reḡes, that is, “Sons of Thunder,”
3.18: and Andri, and Philippos, and Bartholomi, and Mattithyahu, and T’oma, and Ya’aqoḇ of Ḥĕleph, and Taddai, and Shim’on the Kena’anite;
3.19: and Yahuḏah from Qeriyoth, who also delivered Him up. And they went into a house,
3.20: and again the crowd came together, so that they were unable even to eat bread.
3.21: And when His relatives heard about this, they went out to seize Him, for they said, “He is out of His mind.”
3.22: And the scribes who came down from Yerushalayim said, “He has Be’elzebul,” and, “He casts out demons by the ruler of the demons.”
3.23: And calling them near He said to them in parables, “How is Satan able to cast out Satan?
3.24: “And if a malḵuth is divided against itself, that malḵuth is unable to stand.
3.25: “And if a house is divided against itself, that house is unable to stand.
3.26: “And if Satan has risen up against himself, and is divided, he is unable to stand, but has an end.
3.27: “No one is able to enter a strong man’s house and plunder his goods, unless he first binds the strong man, and then he shall plunder his house.
3.28: “Truly, I say to you, all the sins shall be forgiven the sons of men, and whatever blasphemies they speak,
3.29: but he who blasphemes against the Ruaḥ ha’Qodesh has no forgiveness forever, but is subject to everlasting judgment,”
3.30: because they said, “He has an unclean spirit.”
3.31: And His brothers and His mother came, and standing outside they sent to Him, calling Him.
3.32: And a crowd was sitting around Him. And they said to Him, “See, Your mother and Your brothers are outside seeking You.”
3.33: But He answered them, saying, “Who is My mother, or My brothers?”
3.34: And looking about on those sitting round Him, He said, “See My mother and My brothers!
3.35: “For whoever does the desire of Elohim is My brother and My sister and mother.”

4.1: And He began to teach again by the sea, and a large crowd was gathered to Him, so that He entered into a boat, to sit in the sea. And all the crowd was on the land facing the sea.
4.2: And He taught them much in parables, and said to them in His teaching:
4.3: “Listen! See, a sower went out to sow.
4.4: “And it came to be, as he sowed, some fell by the wayside, and the birds of the shamayim came and devoured it.
4.5: “And other fell on rocky places, where it had not much soil. And immediately it sprang up because it had no depth of soil.
4.6: “But when the sun was up it was scorched, and because it had no root it withered away.
4.7: “And other fell among thorns. And the thorns grew up and choked it, and it yielded no crop.
4.8: “And other fell on good soil and yielded a crop that came up, grew and yielded a crop, some thirtyfold, and some sixty, and some a hundred.”
4.9: And He said to them, “He who has ears to hear, let him hear!”
4.10: And when He was alone, those about Him, with the twelve, asked Him about the parable.
4.11: And He said to them, “To you it has been given to know the secret of the Malḵuth of Elohim, but to those who are outside, all are done in parables,
4.12: so that ‘seeing they see but do not perceive, and hearing they hear but do not understand, lest they should turn and their sins be forgiven them.’ ”
4.13: And He said to them, “Do you not understand this parable? How then shall you understand all the parables?
4.15: “These, then, are the ones by the wayside where the Word is sown. And when they hear, Satan comes immediately and takes away the Word that was sown in their hearts.
4.16: “And likewise these are the ones sown on rocky places, who, when they hear the Word, immediately receive it with joy,
4.17: and they have no root in themselves, but are short-lived. Then when pressure or persecution arises because of the Word, immediately they stumble.
4.18: “And others are those sown among thorns, these are they who hear the Word,
4.19: and the worries of this age, and the deceit of riches, and the desires for other matters, entering in, choke the Word, and it becomes fruitless.
4.20: “And those sown on good soil, are those who hear the Word, and accept it, and bear fruit, some thirtyfold, and some sixty, and some a hundred.”
4.21: And He said to them, “Would a lamp be brought to be put under a basket or under a bed? Is it not to be put on a lampstand?
4.22: “For whatever is hidden shall be revealed, and whatever has been kept secret, shall come to light.
4.23: “If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.”
4.24: And He said to them, “Take heed what you hear. With the same measure you use, it shall be measured to you, and more shall be added to you who hear.
4.25: “For whoever possesses, to him more shall be given; but whoever does not possess, even what he possesses shall be taken away from him.”
4.26: And He said, “The Malḵuth of Elohim is as when a man scatters seed on the ground,
4.27: then sleeps by night and rises by day, while the seed sprouts and grows, he himself does not know how.
4.28: “For the soil yields crops by itself: first the blade, then the head, after that the completed grain in the head.
4.29: “And when the crop is ready, immediately he puts in the sickle, because the harvest has come.”
4.30: And He said, “To what shall we compare the Malḵuth of Elohim? Or with what parable shall we present it?
4.31: “Like a mustard seed, which, when it is sown on the ground, is smaller than all the seeds on earth,
4.32: and when it is sown, it grows up and becomes greater than all garden plants, and forms large branches, so that the birds of the shamayim are able to nest under its shade.”
4.33: And with many such parables He was speaking to them the Word as they were able to hear,
4.34: and He was not speaking to them without parables. And when they were alone, He explained all to His talmidim.
4.35: And on the same day, when evening had come, He said to them, “Let us pass over to the other side.”
4.36: And having left the crowd, they took Him along in the boat, as He was. And other little boats were also with Him.
4.37: And there came a great windstorm, and the waves beat into the boat, so that it was already being filled.
4.38: And He was in the stern, asleep on a cushion. And they woke Him up and said to Him, “Teacher, is it no concern to You that we perish?”
4.39: And having been awakened He rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Peace, be still!” And the wind ceased and there was a great calm.
4.40: And He said to them, “Why are you so afraid? Have you not yet belief?”
4.41: And they feared exceedingly, and asked each other, “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey Him!”

5.1: And they came to the other side of the sea, to the country of the Gaḏarenes.
5.2: And when He came out of the boat, immediately there met Him out of the tombs a man with an unclean spirit,
5.3: who had his dwelling among the tombs. And no one was able to bind him, not even with chains,
5.4: because he had often been bound with shackles and chains but the chains had been pulled apart by him, and the shackles broken in pieces, and no one was able to tame him.
5.5: And continually, night and day, he was in the mountains and in the tombs, crying out and cutting himself with stones.
5.6: And seeing 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 from a distance, he ran and bowed down to Him,
5.7: and having called out with a loud voice, said, “What have I to do with You, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, Bĕn of the Most High Ĕl? I adjure You by Elohim not to torture me.”
5.8: For He had said to him, “Come out of the man, unclean spirit!”
5.9: And He was asking him, “What is your name?” And he answered, saying, “My name is Legion, because we are many.”
5.10: And he begged Him very much that He would not send them out of the country.
5.11: Now a great herd of pigs was there, feeding near the mountains.
5.12: And all the demons begged Him, saying, “Send us to the pigs, so that we enter into them.”
5.13: And He gave them permission. And the unclean spirits came out and entered into the pigs - they were about two thousand - and the herd rushed down the steep place into the sea, and drowned in the sea.
5.14: And those who fed the pigs fled, and reported it in the city and in the country. And they went out to see what had taken place.
5.15: So they came to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, and saw the demon-possessed one, him who had the legion, sitting, and dressed, and in his right mind. And they were afraid.
5.16: And those who saw it related to them what was done to the demon-possessed one, and about the pigs.
5.17: And they began to plead with Him to leave their borders.
5.18: And as He was entering into the boat, he who had been demon-possessed begged Him that he might be with Him.
5.19: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 did not allow him, but said to him, “Go home to your friends, and report to them what the Aḏon has done for you, and how He had compassion on you.”
5.20: And he left and began to proclaim in Dekapolis all that 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 had done for him, and all marveled.
5.21: And when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 had passed over again by boat to the other side, a large crowd assembled to Him, and He was by the sea.
5.22: And see, one of the rulers of the congregation came, Ya’ir by name. And when he saw Him, he fell at His feet,
5.23: and begged Him strongly, saying, “My little daughter lies at the point of death. Come, lay Your hands on her to heal her, and she shall live.”
5.24: And He went with him. And a large crowd was following Him, and they were thronging Him.
5.25: And a certain woman had a flow of blood for twelve years,
5.26: and had suffered much from many physicians, and spent all that she had and was no better, but rather became worse.
5.27: Having heard about 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, she came behind Him in the crowd and touched His garment,
5.28: for she said, “If I only touch His garments, I shall be made well.”
5.29: And immediately the fountain of her blood was dried up, and she felt in her body that she was healed of the affliction.
5.30: And immediately 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, knowing in Himself that power had gone out of Him, turned around in the crowd and said, “Who touched My garments?”
5.31: And His talmidim said to Him, “You see the crowd is thronging You, and You say, ‘Who touched Me?’ ”
5.32: And He was looking around to see her who did this.
5.33: And the woman, fearing and trembling, knowing what was done to her, came and fell down before Him and spoke to Him all the truth.
5.34: And He said to her, “Daughter, your belief has healed you. Go in peace, and be relieved from your affliction.”
5.35: While He was still speaking, they came from the ruler of the congregation, saying, “Your daughter is dead. Why trouble the Teacher any further?”
5.36: But having heard the word that was spoken, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to the ruler of the congregation, “Do not be afraid - only believe.”
5.37: And He allowed no one to follow Him except Kĕpha, and Ya’aqoḇ, and Yoḥanan the brother of Ya’aqoḇ.
5.38: So they came to the house of the ruler of the congregation, and He saw a commotion, and much weeping and lamenting.
5.39: And coming in He said to them, “Why make this commotion and weep? The child has not died, but is sleeping.”
5.40: And they were laughing at Him. And when He had put them all out, He took the father and the mother of the child, and those who were with Him, and went in where the child was lying.
5.41: And taking the child by the hand He said to her, “Talitha, qumi,” which is translated, “Little girl, I say to you, arise.”
5.42: And immediately the girl rose up and was walking, for she was twelve years old. And they were completely astonished.
5.43: But He ordered them many times that no one should know it, and said that she should be given to eat.

6.1: And He went away from there and came to His own country, and His talmidim followed Him.
6.2: And Shabbath having come, He began to teach in the congregation. And many who heard were astonished, saying, “Where did He get all this? And what wisdom is this which is given to Him, that such miracles are done through His hands?
6.3: “Is this not the carpenter, the Bĕn of Miryam, and brother of Ya’aqoḇ, and Yosĕph, and Yahuḏah, and Shim’on? And are not His sisters here with us?” And they stumbled in Him.
6.4: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to them, “A naḇi is not unappreciated except in his own country, and among his own relatives, and in his own house.”
6.5: And He was unable to do any miracle there, except that He laid His hands on a few sick ones and healed them.
6.6: And He marveled because of their unbelief. And He was going around among the villages, teaching.
6.7: And He called the twelve near, and began to send them out two by two, and gave them authority over unclean spirits.
6.8: And He instructed them to take naught for the journey except a staff - no bag, no bread, no copper in their money belts,
6.9: but to wear sandals, and not to wear two undergarments.
6.10: And He said to them, “Wherever you enter into a house, stay there until you leave that place.
6.11: “And any place that does not receive you or listen to you, when you leave there, shake off the dust under your feet as a witness against them. Truly, I say to you, it shall be more bearable for Seḏom and Amorah in the day of judgment than for that city!”
6.12: And they went out and proclaimed that people should repent.
6.13: And they were casting out many demons, and they were anointing with oil many who were sick, and they were healing them.
6.14: And Meleḵ Hĕrodĕs heard, for His Name had become well known. And he said, “Yoḥanan the Immerser has been raised from the dead, and because of this these powers are at work in him.”
6.15: Others said, “He is Ĕliyahu.” And others said, “He is a naḇi - like one of the neḇi’im.”
6.16: But when Hĕrodĕs heard, he said, “This one is Yoḥanan whom I beheaded, he has been raised from the dead!”
6.17: For Hĕrodĕs himself had sent and seized Yoḥanan, and bound him in prison because of Hĕrodias, his brother Philippos’ wife, because he had married her,
6.18: for Yoḥanan had said to Hĕrodĕs, “It is not right for you to have your brother’s wife.”
6.19: So Hĕrodias held a grudge against him and wanted to kill him, but was unable,
6.20: for Hĕrodĕs feared Yoḥanan, knowing that he was a righteous and qodesh man, and he protected him. And when he heard him, he was much perplexed, yet heard him gladly.
6.21: And a suitable day came when Hĕrodĕs on his birthday gave a feast for his great men, and the high officers, and the chief men of Galil.
6.22: And when the daughter of Hĕrodias herself came in and danced, and pleased Hĕrodĕs and those who sat with him, the meleḵ said to the girl, “Ask me whatever you want, and I shall give it to you.”
6.23: And he swore to her, “Whatever you ask me, I shall give you, up to half of my malḵuth.”
6.24: And she went out and said to her mother, “What shall I ask?” And she said, “The head of Yoḥanan the Immerser!”
6.25: And coming in immediately with haste to the meleḵ she asked, saying, “I want you to give me at once the head of Yoḥanan the Immerser on a dish.”
6.26: And the meleḵ, becoming deeply grieved, because of the oaths, and because of those who sat with him, did not want to refuse her.
6.27: And the meleḵ straightaway sent an executioner and commanded his head to be brought. And he went and beheaded him in prison,
6.28: and brought his head on a dish, and gave it to the girl. And the girl gave it to her mother.
6.29: And when his talmidim heard of it, they came and took away his dead body and laid it in a tomb.
6.30: And the emissaries gathered to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 and reported to Him all, both what they had done and what they had taught.
6.31: And He said to them, “Come aside by yourselves to a lonely place and rest a little” - for there were many coming and going, and they did not even have time to eat.
6.32: And they went away to a lonely place in the boat by themselves.
6.33: But they saw them going, and many recognized Him and ran there on foot from all the cities, and came before them and came together to Him.
6.34: And having gone out, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 saw a large crowd and was moved with compassion for them because they were like sheep not having a shepherd. And He began to teach them much.
6.35: And as the hour grew late, His talmidim came to Him and said, “This is a lonely place, and now the hour is late.
6.36: “Send them away, so that they go into the surrounding country and villages and buy themselves bread, since they have naught to eat.”
6.37: But He answering, said to them, “You give them to eat.” And they said to Him, “Should we go and buy two hundred silver pieces worth of bread and give them to eat?”
6.38: Then He said to them, “How many loaves do you have? Go and see.” And when they found out they said, “Five, and two fish.”
6.39: And He ordered them to make them all sit down in groups on the green grass.
6.40: And they sat down in groups, in hundreds and in fifties.
6.41: And taking the five loaves and the two fish, looking up to the shamayim, He baraḵ and broke the loaves, and gave them to His talmidim to put before them. And the two fish He divided among them all.
6.42: And all ate and were satisfied.
6.43: And they picked up twelve baskets, filled with pieces, also from the fish.
6.44: Now those who ate the loaves were about five thousand men.
6.45: And immediately He made His talmidim enter into the boat, and to go before Him to the other side, to Bĕyth Tsaiḏa, while He was dismissing the crowd.
6.46: And having sent them away, He went away to the mountain to pray.
6.47: And when evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea. And He was alone on the land.
6.48: And seeing them straining at rowing - for the wind was against them - at about the fourth watch of the night, He came to them walking on the sea, and intended to pass them by.
6.49: And when they saw Him walking on the sea, they thought it was a phantom, and cried out,
6.50: for they all saw Him and were troubled. And immediately He spoke to them and said to them, “Take courage, it is I. Do not be afraid.”
6.51: And He went up to them, into the boat, and the wind ceased. And they were exceedingly amazed in themselves, and marveled.
6.52: For they did not understand about the loaves, because their heart was hardened.
6.53: And having passed over, they came to the land of Gennĕsar and drew to shore.
6.54: And when they came out of the boat, He was immediately recognized,
6.55: and they ran through all that neighborhood, and began to carry about on beds those who were sick to wherever they heard He was.
6.56: And wherever He went, into villages, or cities, or the country, they were laying the sick in the market-places, and begged Him to let them touch if only the tsitsit of His garment. And as many as touched Him were healed.

7.1: And the Pharisees and some of the scribes assembled to Him, having come from Yerushalayim.
7.2: And seeing some of His talmidim eat bread with defiled, that is, with unwashed hands, they found fault.
7.3: For the Pharisees, and all the Yahuḏim, do not eat unless they wash their hands thoroughly, holding fast the tradition of the elders,
7.4: and from the market-place, they do not eat unless they wash. And there are many others which they have received and hold fast - the washing of cups and utensils and copper vessels and couches.
7.5: Then the Pharisees and scribes asked Him, “Why do Your talmidim not walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with unwashed hands?”
7.6: And He answering, said to them, “Well did Yeshayahu naḇa concerning you hypocrites, as it has been written, ‘This people respect Me with their lips, but their heart is far from Me.
7.7: And in vain do they worship Me teaching as teachings the commands of men.’
7.8: “Forsaking the Command of Elohim, you hold fast the tradition of men: washing of pots and cups; and many other like matters you do.”
7.9: And He said to them, “Well do you put aside the Command of Elohim, in order to guard your tradition.
7.10: “For Mosheh said, ‘Respect your father and your mother,’ and, ‘He who curses father or mother, let him be put to death.’
7.11: “But you say, ‘If a man says to his father or mother, “Whatever profit you might have received from me, is Qorban (that is, a gift),” ’
7.12: you no longer let him do anything at all for his father or his mother,
7.13: nullifying the Word of Elohim through your tradition which you have handed down. And many such-like you do.”
7.14: And calling all the crowd to Him, He said to them, “Hear Me, everyone, and understand:
7.15: “There is no matter that enters a man from outside which is able to defile him, but it is what comes out of him that defiles the man.
7.16: “If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear!”
7.17: And when He went from the crowd into a house, His talmidim asked Him concerning the parable.
7.18: And He said to them, “Are you also so without understanding? Do you not perceive that whatever enters a man from outside is unable to defile him,
7.19: because it does not enter his heart but his stomach, and is cast out in the sewer, thus purging all the foods?”
7.20: And He said, “What comes out of a man, that defiles a man.
7.21: “For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil reasonings, adulteries, whorings, murders,
7.22: thefts, greedy desires, wickednesses, deceit, indecency, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness.
7.23: “All this wickedness comes from within and defiles a man.”
7.24: And rising up from there He went to the borders of Tsor and Tsiḏon. And entering into a house He wanted no one to know it, but it was impossible to be hidden.
7.25: For a woman whose young daughter had an unclean spirit heard about Him, and she came and fell at His feet.
7.26: Now the woman was a Yawanite, a Suro-Phoinikĕan by birth, and she kept asking Him to cast the demon out of her daughter.
7.27: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to her, “Let the children be satisfied first, for it is not good to take the children’s bread and throw it to the little dogs.”
7.28: But she answering, said to Him, “Yes, Aḏonai, for even the little dogs under the table eat from the children’s crumbs.”
7.29: And He said to her, “Because of this word go, the demon has gone out of your daughter.”
7.30: And having come into her house, she found the demon gone out, and her daughter lying on the bed.
7.31: And again, going out from the borders of Tsor and Tsiḏon, He came to the Sea of Galil, through the midst of the borders of Dekapolis.
7.32: And they brought to Him one who was deaf and spoke with difficulty, and they begged Him to lay His hand upon him.
7.33: And taking him away from the crowd, He put His fingers in his ears, and having spit, He touched his tongue.
7.34: And looking up to the shamayim, He sighed, and said to him, “Ephphatha,” that is, “Be opened.”
7.35: And immediately his ears were opened, and the binding of his tongue was loosed, and he was speaking plainly.
7.36: And He ordered them, that they should say it to no one, but the more He ordered them, the more they published it.
7.37: And they were immeasurably astonished, saying, “He has done all well. He makes even the deaf to hear and the dumb to speak.”

8.1: In those days, the crowd being very great and having naught to eat, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 called His talmidim near and said to them,
8.2: “I have compassion on the crowd, for they have now been with Me three days and have naught to eat.
8.3: “And if I dismiss them unfed to their home, they shall faint on the way, for some of them have come from afar.”
8.4: And His talmidim answered Him, “How shall anyone be able to feed these people with bread here in the desert?”
8.5: And He asked them, “How many loaves do you have?” And they said, “Seven.”
8.6: And He commanded the crowd to sit down on the ground. And taking the seven loaves, giving thanks, He broke them and gave them to His talmidim to put before them. And they put them before the crowd.
8.7: And they had a few small fish. And having baraḵ, He said to put them also before them.
8.8: And they ate and were satisfied, and they picked up seven large baskets of leftover broken pieces.
8.9: And those eating were about four thousand, and He dismissed them.
8.10: And immediately entering into the boat with His talmidim, He came to the parts of Dalmanutha.
8.11: And the Pharisees came out and began to dispute with Him, seeking from Him a sign from the shamayim, trying Him.
8.12: And sighing deeply in His spirit He said, “Why does this generation seek a sign? Truly, I say to you, no sign shall be given to this generation.”
8.13: And leaving them, again entering into the boat, He went away to the other side.
8.14: And they had forgotten to take bread, and they did not have more than one loaf with them in the boat.
8.15: And He was warning them, saying, “Mind! Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the leaven of Hĕrodĕs.”
8.16: And they were reasoning with one another, saying, “Because we have no bread.”
8.17: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, being aware of it, said to them, “Why do you reason because you have no bread? Do you not yet perceive nor understand? Is your heart still hardened?
8.18: “Having eyes, do you not see? And having ears, do you not hear? And do you not remember?
8.19: “When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many baskets filled with broken pieces did you pick up?” They said to Him, “Twelve.”
8.20: “And when I broke the seven for the four thousand, how many large baskets filled with broken pieces did you pick up?” And they said, “Seven.”
8.21: And He said to them, “How do you not understand?”
8.22: And He came to Bĕyth Tsaiḏa, and they brought a blind man to Him, and begged Him to touch him.
8.23: And taking the blind man by the hand He led him out of the village. And having spit on his eyes, laying hands on him, He asked him, “Do you see at all?”
8.24: And he looked up and said, “I see men like trees, walking.”
8.25: Then He placed His hands on his eyes again and made him look up. And he was restored, and saw all clearly.
8.26: And He sent him away to his home, saying, “Do not go into the village.”
8.27: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 and His talmidim went out to the villages of Kaisereia Philippos. And on the way He asked His talmidim, saying to them, “Who do men say I am?”
8.28: And they said to Him, “Yoḥanan the Immerser, and others, Ĕliyahu, but others, one of the neḇi’im.”
8.29: And He asked them, “And you, who do you say I am?” And Kĕpha answering, said to Him, “You are ha’Mashiaḥ.”
8.30: And He warned them that they should speak to no one about Him.
8.31: And He began to teach them that the Bĕn of Aḏam has to suffer much, and be rejected by the elders and chief kohenim and scribes, and be killed, and after three days to rise again.
8.32: And He was speaking about this openly. Then Kĕpha, taking Him aside, began to rebuke Him.
8.33: And turning around and seeing His talmidim, He rebuked Kĕpha, saying, “Get behind Me, Satan! For your thoughts are not those of Elohim, but those of men.”
8.34: And calling near the crowd with His talmidim, He said to them, “Whoever desires to come after Me, let him deny himself, and take up his stake, and follow Me.
8.35: “For whoever desires to save his life shall lose it, but whoever loses his life for the sake of Me and the Good News, he shall save it.
8.36: “For what shall it profit a man if he gains all the world, and loses his own ḥai?
8.37: “Or what shall a man give in exchange for his life?
8.38: “For whoever is ashamed of Me and My Words in this adulterous and sinning generation, of him the Bĕn of Aḏam also shall be ashamed when He comes in the esteem of His Father with the qodesh messengers.”

9.1: And He said to them, “Truly, I say to you that there are some standing here who shall not taste of death at all until they see the Malḵuth of Elohim having come in power.”
9.2: And after six days 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 took Kĕpha, and Ya’aqoḇ, and Yoḥanan, and led them up on a high mountain alone by themselves. And He was transformed before them.
9.3: And His garments became glittering, exceedingly white, like snow, such as no launderer on earth is able to whiten.
9.4: And there appeared to them Ĕliyahu with Mosheh, and they were talking with 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
9.5: And Kĕpha responding, said to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, “Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. And let us make three booths, one for You, and one for Mosheh, and one for Ĕliyahu,”
9.6: because he did not know what to say, for they were exceedingly afraid.
9.7: And there came a cloud overshadowing them, and a voice came out of the cloud, saying, “This is My Bĕn, the Beloved. Hear Him!”
9.8: And suddenly, looking around, they no longer saw anyone with them, but only 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏.
9.9: And as they were coming down from the mountain, He ordered them not to relate to anyone what they saw, till the Bĕn of Aḏam had risen from the dead.
9.10: And they kept this matter to themselves, debating what the rising from the dead meant.
9.11: And they asked Him, saying, “Why do the scribes say that Ĕliyahu has to come first?”
9.12: And He said to them, “Ĕliyahu indeed, having come first, restores all. And how has it been written concerning the Bĕn of Aḏam, that He is to suffer much and be despised?
9.13: “But I say to you that even Ĕliyahu has come, and they did to him whatever they wanted, as it has been written of him.”
9.14: And coming to the talmidim, He saw a large crowd around them, scribes disputing with them.
9.15: And immediately, when all the crowd saw Him, they were greatly alarmed, and running near, greeted Him.
9.16: And He asked the scribes, “What are you disputing with them?”
9.17: And one of the crowd answering, said, “Teacher, I brought You my son, who has a dumb spirit.
9.18: “And wherever he seizes him, he throws him down, and he froths, and gnashes his teeth, and he wastes away. And I spoke to Your talmidim, that they should cast him out, but they were not able.”
9.19: And He answered him and said, “O unbelieving generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I put up with you? Bring him to Me.”
9.20: So they brought him to Him. And when he saw Him, immediately the spirit threw him into convulsions. And falling on the ground, he rolled about, frothing.
9.21: And He asked his father, “How long has he been like this?” And he said, “From childhood,
9.22: and often he has thrown him both into the fire and into the water to destroy him. But if it is at all possible for You, have compassion on us and help us.”
9.23: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said to him, “If you are able to believe, all is possible to him who believes.”
9.24: And immediately the father of the child cried out and said with tears, “I believe Aḏonai, help my unbelief!”
9.25: And when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 saw that a crowd came running together, He rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to him, “You deaf and dumb spirit, I order you, come out of him, and never again enter into him!”
9.26: And crying out, and convulsing him much, it came out of him. And he became as one dead, so that many said that he was dead.
9.27: But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏, taking him by the hand, lifted him up, and he arose.
9.28: And when He came into a house, His talmidim asked Him separately, “Why were we unable to cast him out?”
9.29: And He said to them, “It is impossible for this kind to come out except through prayer and fasting.”
9.30: And going from there they passed through Galil. And He did not want anyone to know,
9.31: for He was teaching His talmidim and said to them, “The Bĕn of Aḏam is being delivered into the hands of men, and they shall kill Him. And having been killed, He shall rise the third day.”
9.32: But they did not understand the word, and they were afraid to ask Him.
9.33: And they came to Kephar Naḥum, and having come in the house He asked them, “What was it you disputed among yourselves on the way?”
9.34: And they were silent, for on the way they had disputed with one another who was the greatest.
9.35: And sitting down, He called the twelve and said to them, “If anyone wants to be first, he shall be last of all and servant of all.”
9.36: And He took a little child and put him in their midst, and taking him in His arms, He said to them,
9.37: “Whoever receives one of such little children in My Name receives Me. And whoever receives Me, receives not Me, but the One who sent Me.”
9.38: And Yoḥanan said to Him, “Teacher, we saw someone, who does not follow us, casting out demons in Your Name, and we forbade him because he does not follow us.”
9.39: And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤔𐤏 said, “Do not forbid him, for no one who works a miracle in My Name is able to readily speak evil of Me.
9.40: “For he who is not against us is for us.
9.41: “For whoever gives you a cup of water to drink in My Name, because you are of Mashiaḥ, truly, I say to you, he shall by no means lose his reward.
9.42: “And whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in Me to stumble, it is better for him if a millstone were hung around his neck, and he were thrown into the sea.
9.43: “And if your hand makes you stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter into life crippled, than having two hands, to go into Gĕy-Hinnom, into the unquenchable fire,
9.44: where ‘their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.’
9.45: “And if your foot makes you stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter into life crippled, than having two feet, to be thrown into Gĕy-Hinnom, into the unquenchable fire,
9.46: where ‘their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.’
9.47: “And if your eye makes you stumble, pluck it out. It is better for you to enter into the Malḵuth of Elohim with one eye, than having two eyes, to be thrown into the fire of Gĕy-Hinnom,
9.48: where ‘their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.’
9.49: “For everyone shall be seasoned with fire, and every offering shall be seasoned with salt.
9.50: “Salt is good, but if the salt becomes tasteless, how shall you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace among one another.”
